### 🎯 Summary

This PR adjusts the reverse futility pruning return value to be softly tilted towards static evaluation, rather than just the upper bound (`beta`) as it was before. This pull request introduces updates to the Storybook configuration, adds a new script for automating story creation, and implements a new "Video Player" component. The changes enhance developer productivity, improve maintainability, and expand the component library with a customizable video player.

### Storybook Configuration Updates:
* Refactored the `viewports` object in `.storybook/globals.js` for improved readability by formatting each viewport entry onto multiple lines.
* Added a new entry for the "Video Player" component in the `figmaLinks` object in `.storybook/globals.js`, linking to its design resources.

### New Automation Script:
* Introduced a new `add_story.sh` script to automate the creation of new Storybook stories. This script ensures consistent naming conventions (PascalCase), prevents overwriting existing components, and generates the necessary folder and file structure.
* Updated `package.json` to include a new `add-story` npm script for running the `add_story.sh` script.

### New Component: Video Player:
* Added a new `VideoPlayer` component with a Storybook story (`VideoPlayer.stories.js`) and documentation (`VideoPlayer.mdx`). The component supports embedding videos from Vimeo and YouTube with customizable layout, alignment, and other options. body: close #7789 This would solve the scenario highlighted in this issue of a single child whitespace-only text node being wiped, and would also more generically handle scenarios like: ` Value ` where the whitespace is currently wiped in `preserve` mode perhaps unexpectedly. Furthermore, I think this behavior change would also closer align with the documented behavior: https://vuejs.org/api/application#app-config-compileroptions-whitespace > 2. Whitespace characters between elements that contain newlines are removed. > [...] > > Setting this option to 'preserve' will disable (2) and (3). This is definitely a more "radical" solution compared to other ones proposed. Some notes/acknowledgements: 1. This is a breaking change 2. This makes the `preserve` behavior different from Vue 2 `preserve` behavior (e.g. Vue 2.7.14 strips ` ` to `` in preserve mode) 3. This will make bundle sizes larger for users using `whitespace: 'preserve'` due to extra whitespace nodes ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Improved whitespace handling in templates to better preserve or condense spaces for root vs nested elements under the "preserve" strategy. * **Tests** * Expanded and refined test coverage for whitespace scenarios (comments, newlines, pure-whitespace nodes) and an implicit default-slot layout. * Updated end-to-end snapshots to include expected surrounding whitespace in transition tests.

author: reese159
body:
I've been primarily working on test notebooks to make sure I can implement the most basic versions of all the features I have planned, sans the UI. 

I tested a few different text summarization methods, one of them being the GPT integration via the openAI API per your recommendation (see open_ai_text_sumarization.ipynb). It was my first time managing a paid API token like that, so it was an interesting process and took a little bit of time to set up, but it seems to be working really well and I'll probably be using it moving forward. 

I have a couple of decent alternatives that I've identified (see text_summarization.ipynb for my tests), and I'm considering using them as backups in case the funds in my API key ever run out.

As for the meat and potatoes, the actual voice blending and text-to-speech generation, I have a hardcoded working prototype (see voice_blending.ipynb) that generates a small text narration from a blend of  a couple of voices I downloaded locally and added to the git repo. That actually leads me into my biggest question for this PR, and one that I think I spent too much time thinking about instead of actually just getting down to business - is it alright for me to upload the Kokoro-82M voice tensors to my repository? They’re all relatively small files, about 512kb each, so they shouldn’t cause any issues with size and I’d prefer to provide them all in my repository directly. All these files are available publicly at the hugging face repository under the apache 2.0 license (https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M/tree/main/voices), and I linked to it in the ReadMe, but I still think it would be nice for easy access for everything to be available directly in the repository. There is a method to download and cache the files using the “huggingface_hub” api that I found after some research, but I’d rather not have to run that any time a user selects a new tensor when I could simply include them as assets in the repository instead.

Aside from that, everything seems to be going well on my end, feel free to ask any additional questions though! I’m planning on implementing the rest of the features I outlined in my mockup (e.g. file reading, condensing output audio files), adding user input, and tying the features together in python modules next, but please let me know if there is something else you think I should focus on in the meantime.

Thanks as always!
 - Reese

body:
## [COGF-45] Descrição
Foram implementadas novas páginas, funcionalidades e melhorias de UX/UI.

# Pull Request – Atualizações de Variáveis de Ambiente, UI, Formulários e Componentes

Este *pull request* introduz diversas mudanças no código, com foco em melhorias de variáveis de ambiente, aprimoramentos na interface do usuário, nova funcionalidade de componentes e tratamento de formulários. Abaixo estão os destaques organizados por tema.

---

### 🌐 Atualizações de Variáveis de Ambiente
- Renomeado `CLIENT_API_ROOT` para `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_ROOT` nos arquivos `.env.example`, `README.md` e `docker-compose.yml` para seguir as convenções do Next.js sobre variáveis públicas.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a3046da0d15a27e89f2afe639b25748a7ad4d9290af3e7b1b6c1a5533c8f0a8cL2-R2)  
  [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L32-R32)  
  [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L9-R9)

---

### 🎨 Melhorias na Interface do Usuário
- Atualizado o `Button.scss` com estilos para botões `.error.filled`, melhorando o visual de estados de erro.
- Componente `Container` aprimorado com uma opção `fullwidth` e estilos correspondentes para dar mais flexibilidade ao layout.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-466515f9e2fea21e918a56698e2ab4c5ae28ca2628d8bdda0d61f2b172f2c913L13-R17)  
  [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-23e12d7514a26f5e1194a9718f250a8aedf912b4f174ee822ad201721361aac1R7-R11)

---

### 📋 Melhorias no Tratamento de Formulários
- Estendido o `FormProvider` para:
  - Gerenciar erros de resposta,
  - Lidar com envios assíncronos,
  - Resetar o estado do formulário após sucesso.
- Adicionado componente `ErrorTile` para exibir erros de submissão.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c19f7cf8b28400106cd45275cb18cc5bbd1251b7bac3279484449bf0871a4dcL2-R40)  
  [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c19f7cf8b28400106cd45275cb18cc5bbd1251b7bac3279484449bf0871a4dcL25-R102)

- `FormInput` agora suporta upload de arquivos e tipos adicionais de input, tornando os formulários mais versáteis.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-512995e58cf258a08c76e48de3ce10aa11e2108773a37344bf456787bd22fc1eL1-R32)  
  [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-512995e58cf258a08c76e48de3ce10aa11e2108773a37344bf456787bd22fc1eR41-R48)

---

### 🧩 Novos Componentes
- Criado o componente `MyProfileContent` para gerenciar perfis de usuários, incluindo:
  - Exibição de dados do usuário,
  - Listagem de produtos,
  - Ações para gerenciamento de produtos.

---

### 📚 Atualizações na Documentação
- Comentários JSDoc adicionados a diversos componentes (`Spinner`, `LoginContent`, `FormInput`) para melhorar a compreensão e manutenção por desenvolvedores.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ae166d17573d2b7c5fc8716c29ac84f8d927faa139f81b2117c12098025ccacaR1-R7)  
  [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-41d01e8ceba268387c428b44ca3f24b9770dcfeba2af7b1d97d6a90290a0b279R5-R10)  
  [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-512995e58cf258a08c76e48de3ce10aa11e2108773a37344bf456787bd22fc1eL1-R32)

---

### ✅ Conclusão
Essas mudanças trazem melhorias significativas à organização das variáveis de ambiente, flexibilidade da UI, robustez no tratamento de formulários e legibilidade do código, além de facilitar o trabalho da equipe de desenvolvimento.

---
### Tasks
* [COGF-54] Docstrings nos componentes que estão sem (#46)
Adicionado as docstrings

* [COGF-46] Borda inferior no tiles de produto (#47)
Implementado a borda inferior para o tile de produto e o card dos formulários de login.

* [COGF-51] Tratamento de erros nos formulários (#48)
Criei os elementos necessários para o tratamento de errors e apliquei para exibitr as mensagens vindas do backend.

* [COGF-52] Estilo de botão no "Exemple de JSON" (#49)
Adicionei cursor pointer e preveni a seleção de text que estava atrapalhando a experiencia do usuário

* [COGF-53] Erros nas variaveis de ambiente (#50)
Implementando variavle pública do nextjs para quando for rodar incluir nos arquivas env

* [COGF-56] Colocar as funções de login e cadastro dentro do AuthContext (#51)
Agora as funcções de login e cadastro fazem parte to AuthContext

* [COGF-49] Logout de usuário (#52)
Criei o botão para o usuário sair da conta.

* [COGF-47] Página de perfil do usuário (#53)
Criado a página de perfil do usuário.

* [COGF-48] Página de cadastro de produtos (#54)
Criada a página para criar novos produtos e também foi criado e melhorado alguns outros componentes necessários.

* [COGF-48] Página de cadastro de produtos (#55)
Criada a página para criar novos produtos e também foi criado e melhorado alguns outros componentes necessários.

* [COGF-57] Editar produto (#56)
Foi criado a página para editar o produto.

author: mchris2
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the `SafeCleanupCDrive` project, including enhancements to functionality, documentation, and user experience. Key changes involve improvements to user profile handling, new features for cleanup operations, and expanded documentation for installation, usage, and troubleshooting.

### Functional Enhancements:
* Converted `Get-UserProfileType` and `Get-UserProfiles` to an inclusion-based approach for more accurate filtering of user profiles. Added `Get-ProfileInfo` to identify large or inactive profiles, with reporting functionality for excluded profiles.
* Centralized user profile discovery and filtering, improving account type detection and enabling explicit control over cleanup steps via the `AccountTypes` array in `$CleanupConfig`.
* Enhanced LDAP lookup logic to handle domain accounts and excluded service/system profiles reliably. Improved SID mapping for folders in `C:\Users`.

### Documentation Improvements:
* Expanded `README.md` with prerequisites, installation instructions, usage examples, detailed descriptions of cleanup actions, and troubleshooting tips. Added sections on contributing, licensing, and contact information.
* Clarified default states and switches for cleanup actions, including new options like `-CleanupOrphanedProfiles` and `-LogFilePath`.

### Bug Fixes:
* Resolved issues with incorrect processing of local, service, or renamed system accounts and improved handling of profiles missing from WMI/CIM lists.
* Corrected domain profile username extraction for cases with dots in usernames or domain names.

body:
This pull request addresses a NullPointerException that occurs in the simulateNullPointerException method. The exception was caused by attempting to call length() on a String object that could be null. To resolve this, a null check has been added before invoking the length() method. This ensures that the code handles null values gracefully and prevents runtime crashes.

Alternatively, the fix could use Objects.requireNonNull(str) to fail fast with a clear error message, but for now, a standard null check is implemented to handle the null case appropriately.

Please review the changes and let me know if further adjustments are needed.

body:
### Description

While running integration tests manually, I have noticed that single test methods often required an unexpectedly long time to execute, often around 5 seconds, sometimes 10 seconds or 15 seconds. This is significantly too long, these methods should execute within a few milliseconds. It is also interesting that the runtime is always close to a multiple of 5 seconds.

Testing has shown that the `close()` method of `RestHighLevelClient` incurs this delay, indirectly, while shutting down the `PoolingAsyncClientConnectionManager`.

I have tried a couple of approaches to fix this, but none proved really good/feasible in the end. Thus, here's just a quick fix which executes the `close()` method asynchronously. That fixes the delay.

* Category: Test fix
* Why these changes are required? Tests require an unproportionally long time to execute

This PR implements a new DatePicker component for the Giftee Abukuma Design System, following the specifications in GitHub issue #581.

## 🎯 Overview

The DatePicker component provides a native HTML5 date input with a calendar icon overlay, similar to how the Select component uses a dropdown arrow. The implementation follows existing design system patterns and includes both CSS and React package implementations.

- **Native HTML5 date input** for cross-platform compatibility and accessibility

body:
# Add Python Testing Infrastructure

## Summary

This PR sets up a comprehensive testing infrastructure for the BERT NLP project using Poetry as the package manager and pytest as the testing framework. The infrastructure provides everything needed to start writing and running tests immediately.

## Changes Made

### Package Management
- ✅ Set up Poetry as the project's package manager
- ✅ Created `pyproject.toml` with complete project configuration
- ✅ Added testing dependencies as development dependencies:
  - `pytest` (^7.4.3) - Core testing framework
  - `pytest-cov` (^4.1.0) - Coverage reporting
  - `pytest-mock` (^3.12.0) - Mocking utilities

### Testing Configuration
- ✅ Configured pytest in `pyproject.toml` with:
  - Custom markers: `unit`, `integration`, `slow`
  - Coverage reporting (HTML, XML, terminal)
  - Coverage threshold set to 0% (to be increased to 80% when tests are added)
  - Strict mode and comprehensive test discovery patterns

### Directory Structure
```
tests/
├── __init__.py
├── conftest.py          # Shared fixtures
├── test_infrastructure_validation.py
├── unit/
│   └── __init__.py
└── integration/
    └── __init__.py
```

### Testing Fixtures (conftest.py)
Created reusable fixtures for common testing needs:
- `temp_dir` - Temporary directory management
- `mock_config` - Mock configuration objects
- `mock_model` - Mock model for testing
- `sample_text_data` - Sample text data
- `sample_tokenized_data` - Sample tokenized data
- `mock_data_loader` - Mock data loader
- `capture_stdout` - Stdout capture for testing print statements
- `reset_random_seeds` - Automatic random seed reset for reproducibility

### Additional Setup
- ✅ Created `.gitignore` with comprehensive Python/testing patterns
- ✅ Updated `CLAUDE.md` with testing commands and project structure
- ✅ Created validation tests to verify the infrastructure works

## How to Use

### Install Dependencies
```bash
poetry install
```

### Run Tests
```bash
# Run all tests
poetry run test
# or
poetry run tests

# Run with verbose output
poetry run pytest -v

# Run only unit tests
poetry run pytest tests/unit

# Run only integration tests
poetry run pytest tests/integration

# Run tests with specific marker
poetry run pytest -m unit

# Run with coverage report
poetry run pytest --cov
```

### Writing Tests
1. Place unit tests in `tests/unit/`
2. Place integration tests in `tests/integration/`
3. Use the fixtures from `conftest.py` for common testing needs
4. Mark tests appropriately with `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration`, or `@pytest.mark.slow`

## Notes

- Coverage threshold is currently set to 0% to allow initial setup. This should be increased to 80% once actual tests are written
- The infrastructure validation tests confirm that all components are working correctly
- Poetry lock file (`poetry.lock`) is not gitignored and should be committed to ensure reproducible builds
- All test commands are available through Poetry scripts for consistency

## Next Steps

1. Start writing unit tests for existing modules
2. Add integration tests for end-to-end workflows
3. Increase coverage threshold to 80% once sufficient tests are written
4. Consider adding additional testing tools as needed (e.g., hypothesis for property-based testing)

pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change replaces the usage of [`java.io.File#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/io/File.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)) with [`java.nio.file.Files#createTempFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/file/Files.html#createTempFile(java.lang.String,java.lang.String,java.nio.file.attribute.FileAttribute...)) which has more secure attributes.

The `java.io.File#createTempFile()` method creates a file that is world-readable and world-writeable, which is almost never necessary. Also, the file created is placed in a predictable directory (e.g., `/tmp`). Having predictable file names, locations, and will lead to many types of vulnerabilities. History has shown that this insecure pattern can lead to [information leakage](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-28168/), [privilege escalation](https://www.cvedetails.com/cve/CVE-2021-29428/) and even [code execution](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2022/02/25/3).

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
+  import java.nio.file.Files;
   ...
-  File txtFile = File.createTempFile("acme", ".txt");
+  File txtFile = Files.createTempFile("acme", ".txt").toFile();
```

author: calvingiles
body:
# What happens

At present, when multiple function responses are provided for the same function call in different events AND those responses occur in parallel with responses for function responses that do not correlate then the event re-writing logic can incorrectly include too many function responses, resulting in as error like:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Please ensure that the number of function response parts is equal to the number of function call parts of the function call turn.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT"
}
```

# What should happen

The perfect solution to this scenario is a little complex and unclear, but a few things should be true:

1. when processing the events into contents, the result should always be a valid model input.
2. If multiple function CALLS are present with the same ID, take the most recent as the only call.
3.  If multiple function RESPONSES are present, take the most recent as the only response.
4.  If calls are present in parallel, while moving one to ensure the above should not automatically move the others.
5.  If responses are present in parallel, while moving one to ensure the above should not automatically move the others.
6.  If multiple calls should occur in a sequence, they should be collected into a parallel call
7.  If multiple responses should occur in a sequence, they should be collected into a parallel response

Note: points 6 and 7 seem to suggest that models MUST support parallel function calling, and that this would break with models that don't. This is not in fact a requirement as the only way for these above re-writing rules to bring multiple responses together is if a series of function responses were to be ordered together with no model parts interleaved - i.e. there must be parallel function responses already present to bring this about. Regarding parallel calls, since the above logic will always bring a matching number of calls to responses into the preceding turn, parallel function calling requires parallel responses to already exist. The other situation for parallel calls is when unmatched - which should only occur naturally at the end of a conversation, and in these cases they would also need to already be present to be returned as such.

# Solution

A new `_extract_latest_function_parts` method that performs direct creation of the `contents` according to these rules.

The function calls and responses are special cased and manipulated. All other parts are kept as they were. This leaves all auth and other invalid event filtering logic in place, as well as foreign agent part re-writing.

# Code source

All tests and proposed implementation were coded without AI, so there is negligible likelihood that these snippets of code exist anywhere in copyrighted source code.

# Update - added validation

I have added an additional validator to the mock model and tests to catch scenarios where this problem occurs in the future.

body:
## Issue - resolve: SQL injection vulnerability in PostgreSQL SQL generation functions ## Why is this change needed? The code directly interpolated table and column names into SQL statements without proper escaping or validation. In PostgreSQL SQL generation functions, tableName and column.name were directly inserted into SQL strings. If these values contain special characters, SQL keywords, or malicious content, it could lead to SQL injection vulnerabilities. ## What would you like reviewers to focus on? - The implementation of the `escapeIdentifier` function for PostgreSQL identifier escaping - Proper application of identifier escaping across all SQL generation functions - Test coverage and snapshot updates to ensure the security fix doesn't break existing functionality - Performance impact of the escaping function (should be minimal) ## Testing Verification - All existing tests pass with updated snapshots - TypeScript compilation succeeds without errors - Linting passes all checks - Manual verification that generated SQL properly escapes identifiers with double quotes ## What was done ### 🤖 Generated by PR Agent at 65e58f0212ee73b1c03855c8ba556f147b6a3d4d - Fix PostgreSQL SQL injection vulnerability in identifier handling - Add `escapeIdentifier` function to properly quote table/column names - Update all SQL generation functions to use escaped identifiers - Update test snapshots to reflect proper identifier quoting ## Detailed Changes

The fix uses PostgreSQL's standard identifier quoting mechanism (double quotes) and properly escapes any internal double quotes by doubling them. **Security Impact Examples:** - Malicious table name: `users; DROP TABLE sensitive_data; --` would previously allow arbitrary SQL execution - Malicious column name: `id; INSERT INTO logs VALUES ('hacked'); --` could inject additional SQL commands **Before:** ```sql CREATE TABLE users (id bigint PRIMARY KEY, email varchar(255)); ``` **After:** ```sql CREATE TABLE "users" ("id" bigint PRIMARY KEY, "email" varchar(255)); ``` ___ >

author: marty-sullivan
body:
## Summary

This PR adds improvements to the AWS credential that address both security best practices and allows for advanced AWS access patterns, like enabling cross-account AWS access on behalf of the user's credentials, or the n8n server.

The current implementation only allows for IAM User Access Key / Secret Key (or temporary credentials that will need to be constantly refreshed). This pattern is against AWS's best practice recommendations to have workloads that assume an IAM Role rather than rely on long-lived credentials:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#bp-workloads-use-roles
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/v1/userguide/cli-configure-role.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com#cli-role-prepare

To address this, I've added a new feature to the AWS Credential. Once PR is reviewed and merged, I will gladly add documentation.

Summary:

1. Add a toggle for "Credential Type" which by default is the existing options for `IAM Access Key` and new option for `Assume IAM Role`

2. For Role Assumption: 

- the user must provide a Role ARN, an ExternalID (to address the "Confused Deputy" problem) and a Session Name
- the user can choose to "Use System Credentials for STS Call" if the n8n administrator has configured AWS credentials in the environment variables OR in an EC2/ECS/EKS role on the n8n server. The system creds must have permission to assume roles on behalf of any n8n users and should require an external id to be configured. (The system credentials will never be used for anything but `sts.AssumeRole` by this credential, users must not be allowed to use the system creds for workflows)
- the user can also choose to provide an Access Key & Secret Key that is used to perform the STS AssumeRole call if the administrator has not configured system AWS credentials. 

⚠️ Note about External ID: This should actually be something unique that n8n generates per-credential and displays to the user, and not something the user is able to configure. I couldn't figure out a way to make the credential editor do something like this though (generate a value that is used as part of the credential and display it read-only to the user). Instead, I've documented this deviation from best practice and suggest to the user that the External ID they generate on their own should be treated as a secret from any other users they don't trust within the same n8n instance. This is not ideal but is the best I can come up with.

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/apn/securely-using-external-id-for-accessing-aws-accounts-owned-by-others/

3. For IAM Access Key:

- the behavior is still the same and is backward compatible with existing AWS credentials
- I have created several unit tests that show existing credentials should continue working fine, but someone else might want to review too

![aws_credential](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acec3b3b-56e5-4038-9601-73ae77288cd8)

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

author: blixibon
body:
HL2MP bots have unfinished support for using `item_healthcharger` and `func_healthcharger` entities to heal themselves. This pull request allows them to be supported to the same extent as regular health kits.

Specific changes made:

- Chargers with no juice are not considered when searching for health kits.
- Bots navigate to a point in front of the chargers, rather than directly into the chargers.
	- Positions can be displayed using `hl2mp_bot_debug_health_scavenging`, which was previously unused.
- Chargers are now identified by finding `item_health*`/`func_health*` and then searching for "charger" in the classname directly, rather than through leading wildcards with `*charger*`/`*_health*`, which Source does not support by default.
	- Previously, this was causing the health entity filter to evaluate *all* entities, and for all health kits to be considered chargers. The latter was not noticeable due to the health kits being consumed before any charger-related actions could take place.
- Range increased from `50` to the actual player use radius, which is `80` by default.
- Bots drop any prop they're holding with the gravity gun before interacting with a charger.
- Bots now look at the charger while using it.
- Bots now press the +USE button rather than invoking the chargers' `Use()` functions directly, as the latter had issues.
- Critical health now uses the correct comparison operator when deciding whether to abandon a charger.
- Bots will only abandon a charger they're currently using due to a threat if there is a clear path between them and the threat.
- Chargers are not considered when the bot has a visible enemy and is not at critical health. If the bot is currently moving to a charger, it will abandon it.
	- This is partially based on the existing check for when a bot is already using the charger, and this prevents the bot from getting caught in a loop.
- Bots on "Expert" difficulty will now move left and right while using a charger to avoid standing still. This behavior can be toggled with `hl2mp_bot_health_charger_weave`.

Here's a video of how health scavenging behavior worked prior to this pull request:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6b1c5f7-1155-4cd7-8f54-e08359c45396

Here's a video showing how it works with the changes included:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa6121f5-396e-4246-96fa-a3f0cdcb8b4d

Here's a video showing a bot on "Expert" difficulty using the aforementioned "weaving" behavior:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96617a09-b412-400a-86d1-d195ece47bb1

## About The Pull Request

<!-- Describe your pull request. Avoid text walls, use concise bullet points for easier readability. Document every change, or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR. -->

I've been told by certain Psydonites that the old faith's been missing a lot of flavour and features in the time since the heyday of the ChatGPT'd Ten. To rectify that I've given them a few features:

- A Unique Conversion T1 Miracle
- T1-T3 miracles reminiscent of their classic Roguetown incarnations
- A mood buff and protection from curses if they dare to don the heretical psycross in public
- Churn undead can no longer be resisted by ordinary, 'young' vampires and zombies as it's meant to be a hard counter to undead.
- Psydon people shout a special line when churning undead

## Testing Evidence

## Why It's Good For The Game

<!-- Argue for the merits of your changes and how they benefit the game, especially if they are controversial. If you can't, then it probably isn't good for the game in the first place. -->

From an OOC perspective, now that Psydonism is heretical, it's probably a good idea to give people a reason to play the proscribed Psydonians. I also wanted to experiment with giving them a spell list reminiscent of the pre-Raytown days where the main benefit to being a Psydonian came from the passive benefits of being one - such as worn psicrosses offering you protection from those kinds of evils ontologically opposite of the light. 

Overall, I think I've done a decent job of finally giving Psydonism a proper niche within the scheme of (modern) heterodoxy.

author: usn757
body:
### **1. 작업 개요**

본 PR은 사용자가 좌석을 선택하여 예매하고, 결제를 준비하며, 필요시 예매를 취소하는 **예매 시스템의 핵심 End-to-End 흐름을 구현**하는 것을 목표로 합니다.

안정적이고 확장 가능한 예매 기능을 구현하기 위해, 기존 도메인 모델의 구조를 개선하는 **대규모 리팩토링을 병행**했습니다. `Booking` 관련 도메인을 전용 패키지로 분리하고, `Venue` 및 `Seat`를 마스터 데이터로 격리하여 각 도메인의 역할과 책임을 명확히 했습니다.

### **2. 주요 작업 내용**

* **예매 핵심 기능 구현:**
    * `결제 대기` 상태의 예매를 생성하고, 토스페이먼츠 연동에 필요한 정보를 반환하는 API 구현 (`BookingController`, `Service`, `DTO` 생성)
    * 예매를 취소하는 비즈니스 로직 및 API 구현
* **도메인 구조 재설계 및 리팩토링:**
    * **Booking 도메인 분리:** `Booking`, `Ticket` 등 관련 클래스를 `booking` 전용 패키지로 이동하여 응집도 향상
    * **Venue 도메인 분리:** `Venue`, `Seat` 엔티티를 `venue` 마스터 데이터용 패키지로 분리하여 도메인 경계 명확화
* **엔티티 안정성 강화:**
    * `Booking` 엔티티의 `@Setter`를 제거하고 비즈니스 메서드를 사용하도록 강제하여 캡슐화 강화
    * `Ticket` 생성 시 `price`가 누락되던 치명적 버그 수정
    * 양방향 연관관계 편의 메서드(`setTickets`)를 추가하여 객체 상태의 일관성 보장
* **데이터 무결성 확보:**
    * `ConcertSeat`, `Ticket` 등에 `UNIQUE` 제약조건을 추가하여 중복 예매 및 데이터 오염 가능성을 원천 차단

### **3. 주요 변경사항**

✨ **새로 추가된 파일:**
* `booking/controller/BookingController.java`
* `booking/service/BookingService.java`
* `booking/dto/BookingDTO.java`
* `venue/repository/VenueRepository.java`, `SeatRepository.java`
* `_global/exception/ErrorCode.java`에 `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_CANCELED_BOOKING` 추가

🚚 **이동 및 대폭 수정된 파일:**
* `booking/domain/Booking.java` (패키지 이동, `@Setter` 제거, 메서드 추가 등)
* `booking/domain/Ticket.java` (패키지 이동, 가격 누락 버그 수정)
* `venue/domain/Venue.java` (패키지 이동)
* `venue/domain/Seat.java` (패키지 이동)
* `concert/domain/ConcertSeat.java` (`Ticket`과의 관계를 `@OneToOne`으로 수정)
* 기타 도메인 이동에 따라 의존성 수정이 필요한 다수 파일의 `import` 경로 업데이트

### **4. 관련 이슈**

### **5. 추가 정보 (리뷰어를 위한 가이드)**

이번 PR은 단순 기능 추가를 넘어, 시스템의 뼈대를 바로잡는 중요한 변경들을 포함하고 있습니다. 리뷰 시 아래의 흐름을 따라가시면 변경 사항의 의도를 파악하시는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.

#### **1. 도메인 구조 재설계의 필연성**
* **문제점:** 예매 기능을 구현하기에 앞서, `Booking`, `Venue`, `Seat` 등의 핵심 개념들이 `concert` 도메인에 혼재되어 있어 책임과 경계가 불분명했습니다.
* **해결책:** 안정적인 기능 구현을 위해 **선제적으로 도메인 리팩토링을 단행**했습니다. `Booking`과 `Venue`를 각각의 독립된 패키지로 분리하여, 향후 각 도메인이 확장될 때 다른 곳에 미치는 영향을 최소화하는 견고한 기반을 마련했습니다.

#### **2. 예매 생성부터 결제 준비까지의 흐름 (핵심 기능)**
* `BookingController`는 `createBooking` 요청을 받으면 `BookingService`를 호출합니다.
* `BookingService`는 좌석 선점 검증 후, `Booking` 엔티티를 **`PENDING_PAYMENT` 상태로 DB에 저장**합니다.
* **중요:** 서비스는 JPA 엔티티를 그대로 반환하는 대신, 컨트롤러와 약속된 **`BookingDTO.PaymentReadyResponse` DTO를 직접 생성하여 반환**합니다. 이 DTO에는 토스페이먼츠 `requestPayment` SDK 호출에 필요한 `orderId`, `orderName`, `amount` 등이 모두 포함되어 있습니다.
* 이를 통해 **Controller는 DTO 변환 책임 없이 오직 HTTP 통신에만 집중**할 수 있으며, **`LazyInitializationException`과 같은 잠재적 위험을 원천 차단**했습니다.

#### **3. 예매 취소 처리 전략 ('이관 후 삭제')**
* **딜레마:** 예매 취소 시, ① 취소된 좌석은 다른 사람이 즉시 예매할 수 있어야 하고(자원 반환), ② 취소 기록은 영구적으로 보존되어야 합니다.
* **해결책:** `cancelBooking` 메서드는 이 두 가지 상충하는 요구사항을 모두 만족시키기 위해 **'이관 후 삭제' 패턴**을 적용했습니다.
    1.  취소할 `Booking`과 `Ticket` 정보를 `History` 테이블로 옮기는 것을 시뮬레이션하고(`archiveBookingAndTickets`),
    2.  `tickets.concert_seat_id`의 `UNIQUE` 제약조건을 해제하기 위해 운영 DB에서 해당 레코드를 물리적으로 삭제합니다.
* 이를 통해 좌석의 재사용성과 데이터 보존이라는 두 마리 토끼를 모두 잡았습니다.

#### **4. 엔티티 안정성 강화 (필수 리뷰)**
* **`@Setter` 제거 (`Booking.java`):** 캡슐화를 깨뜨려 데이터 무결성을 해칠 수 있는 `@Setter`를 과감히 제거했습니다. 모든 상태 변경은 이제 `cancel()`, `confirm()`과 같은 의도가 명확한 비즈니스 메서드를 통해서만 가능합니다.
* **가격 누락 버그 수정 (`Ticket.java`):** `Ticket` 생성 시 `price` 필드를 스냅샷으로 저장하는 로직이 누락되어 `NPE`를 유발하던 치명적인 버그를 수정했습니다.

### **6. 향후 개선 제안**
* **결제 완료 처리**: 현재는 '결제 대기' 상태의 예매만 생성합니다. 토스페이먼츠의 **결제 성공 웹훅(Webhook)** 을 수신하여 예매 상태를 `CONFIRMED`로 변경하고, 실제 결제 정보를 `Payment` 엔티티에 저장하는 로직 구현이 필요합니다.
* **히스토리 테이블 구현**: `archiveBookingAndTickets` 메서드의 `// TODO` 주석에 명시된 대로, 실제 `BookingHistory`, `TicketHistory` 테이블 및 Repository를 구현하여 데이터 이관 로직을 완성해야 합니다.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

`DDEntryPoint` activates created spans so `DDSpan` should too.

Activation binds span to current thread via ThreadLocal so it will become incorrect when IO/Fiber switches threads but at least it's an improvement and consistent with root spans.

Ideally there would be a Span option to disable activation entirely like this: https://github.com/typelevel/natchez/pull/1187

author: ibukun-ayo
body:
**Description:**
This PR introduces the foundational Clarity smart contract implementation for VaultForge — a Bitcoin-native asset tokenization platform built on the Stacks blockchain. It establishes the full lifecycle for minting collateral-backed NFTs, trading them on a decentralized marketplace, enabling fractional ownership, and integrating intelligent staking with autonomous yield generation.

---

**Key Changes:**

✅ **Protocol Foundations**

* Defined global constants, protocol parameters, and error codes
* Initialized key storage structures for tokens, listings, fractional shares, staking yields

✅ **NFT Tokenization & Validation**

* `mint-asset-token`: Mint collateralized NFTs with URI validation & collateral checks
* `transfer-asset-token`: Secure transfer of ownership (non-staked only)
* Utility functions for safe arithmetic, URI checks, and recipient validation

✅ **Decentralized Marketplace**

* `create-marketplace-listing`: List tokens with price validation and staking constraints
* `execute-token-purchase`: Handles buyer payment, protocol fee extraction, and token transfer with listing deactivation

✅ **Fractional Ownership**

* `transfer-fractional-shares`: Enables share-level transfers with overflow/balance protections

✅ **Staking & Yield Generation**

* `initiate-token-staking`: Activates staking with block tracking
* `terminate-token-staking`: Final reward payout with state reset
* `distribute-staking-rewards`: Calculates and transfers staking rewards based on yield rate and time

✅ **Read-Only Interfaces**

* Query functions for token details, marketplace listings, fractional ownership, staking rewards, and protocol statistics
* `calculate-accumulated-rewards`: Returns real-time staking rewards based on block difference and APY

---

**Impact:**
This implementation enables the VaultForge protocol to:

* Tokenize real-world assets with Bitcoin-backed security
* Provide a permissionless trading experience for NFTs
* Unlock asset liquidity via fractionalization
* Offer sustainable yield for staked assets
* Serve as a DeFi-ready foundation for asset-based financial primitives

---

**Next Steps:**

* Implement access controls (admin config updates)
* Add support for cross-chain oracle data
* Enhance fractional buy/sell flows with automated liquidity
* Develop UI interfaces for interaction and analytics

## Summary
This PR enhances the pruner script to support configuration via environment variables, making it more flexible for different deployment environments  without requiring container rebuilds.

## Changes Made
- **Environment Variable Support**: Added support for `DATA_PATH`, `PRUNE_DAYS`, and `PRUNE_EXCLUDES` with sensible defaults 
- **Day-based Configuration**: Replaced hardcoded 48-hour retention with configurable `PRUNE_DAYS` (default: 2 days)
- **Flexible Exclusions**: Support comma-separated list in `PRUNE_EXCLUDES` for multiple file/folder exclusions
- **Enhanced Logging**: Added configuration logging for better debugging and transparency
- **Docker Integration**: Updated Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml with example configurations

## Environment Variables
- `DATA_PATH` - Path to data directory (default: `/home/hluser/hl/data`)
- `PRUNE_DAYS` - Number of days to retain files (default: `2`)
- `PRUNE_EXCLUDES` - Comma-separated list of files/folders to exclude (default: `visor_child_stderr`)

## Usage Examples
**Docker Compose:**
```yaml 
environment:
  - PRUNE_DAYS=7
  - PRUNE_EXCLUDES=visor_child_stderr,logs,backups
```
**Docker Run:**
docker run -e PRUNE_DAYS=7 -e PRUNE_EXCLUDES=visor_child_stderr,logs

## Backward Compatibility

All changes maintain full backward compatibility. Existing deployments will continue to work with the same behavior (2-day retention, excluding visor_child_stderr).

author: jayesh251
body:
This release has the following changes:

# New Features
1.  Formula-based versions of HH-type channels 
     - Added `HHChannelF` and `HHGateF` for formula-based evaluation of Hodgkin-Huxley type gating parameters
     - Added a formula interface for `HHGate`: Users can now assign string formula in `exprtk` syntax to `alphaExpr`, `betaExpr`, `tauExpr` and `infExpr` to fill up the               tables. These can take either `v` for voltage or `c` for concentration as independent variable names in the formula.
2. Added `moose.sysfields` to display system fields like `fieldIndex`, `numData` etc. 
3. Reintroduced `moose.neighbors()` function to retrieve neighbors on a particular field. This allows more flexibility than `element.neighbors[fieldName]` by allowing the user to specify the message type ("Single", "OneToOne", etc.) and direction (1 for incoming 0 for outgoing, otherwise both directions).

# API Updates
1. API changes in  `moose.vec` and `moose.element,` including updated documentation.
2. `moose.showfields` updated to 
 - skip system fields like `fieldIndex`, `numData` etc. These can now be printed using `sysfields` function.
 -  print common but informative fields like `name`, className`, `tick` and `dt` at the top.
 - return `None` instead of the output string to avoid cluttering the interactive session.
3. `moose.pwe()` returns `None` to avoid output clutter. Use `moose.getCwe()` for retrieving the current working element.
4. `children` field of moose elements (ObjId) now return a list of elements instead of vecs (Id). This brings consistency between `parent` and `children` fields.
5. `moose.le()` returns `None` to avoid output clutter. Use `element.children` field to access the list of children.
6. `path` field for elements (ObjId) now includes the index in brackets, as in the core C++. This avoids confusion with vec (Id) objects.
7. `moose.copy()` now accepts either `str` path or `element` or `vec` for `src` and `dest` parameters.
8. Attempt to access paths with non-existent element now consistently raises RuntimeError.
9. `moose.delete` now accepts vec (Id) as argument.

# Installation
Installing released version from PyPI using `pip`

This version is now available for installation via `pip`. To install the latest release, run
```
pip install pymoose
```

# Documentation
1. Updated `Ubuntu` build instructions for better clarity.
2. Enhanced documentation for `HHGate`, including additional warnings.
3. Updated documentation for `Stoich,` with improved code comments and clarifications.

# Bug Fixes
1. `bool` attribute handling added to `moose.vec`
2. More informative error message for unhandled attributes in `moose.vec`
3. Fixed issue #505
4. `moose.setCwe()` now handles str, element (ObjId) and vec (Id) parameters correctly
5. fixed `moose.showmsg()` mixing up incoming and outgoing messages.

body:
# PR Description: Add SafeLMCacheConnectorV1 for Non-Critical LMCache Integration

## Purpose

Add SafeLMCacheConnectorV1, a circuit breaker wrapper that prevents vLLM failures when LMCache is unavailable. This makes LMCache non-critical - vLLM continues serving requests using native caching when LMCache fails, and automatically recovers when service is restored.

Fixes the issue where LMCache service problems cause complete vLLM system failures.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Test with safe connector
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SafeLMCacheConnectorV1", "kv_role":"kv_both"}'

# Break LMCache service (stop daemon, network issues)
# Verify vLLM continues working

# Restore LMCache service  
# Verify automatic recovery
```

## Test Result

**Circuit Breaker Working:**
- Opens after 3 LMCache failures
- vLLM continues processing requests without crashes
- Automatic recovery when LMCache service restored
- Sub-millisecond overhead during normal operation

**System Resilience:**
- Zero system failures during LMCache outages
- Graceful fallback to native vLLM caching
- Self-healing with exponential backoff (30-300s)

## (Optional) Documentation Update

None required. Drop-in replacement for LMCacheConnectorV1 with identical API.

author: zucchini-nlp
body:
# What does this PR do?

As per title, refactors attention implementation setting and makes it a public API. We should encourage users to `model.set_attn_implementation()` whenever they want to change it after loading the model, instead of setting config's private attr `model.config._attn_implementation="sdpa"`

After the clean-up, we will be calling attention implementation setter only once per pretrained model class, when init the module. Since `from_pretrained/from_config` at the end call `init`, we don't need to keep it as a `classmethod`. Also setting attention after init allows us to know which backbones support attn or do not, and might be useful of we want to early raise errors in the future versions.

Also, removed redundant flags for FA2/FA3. Realized that we can use one flag for both versions :)

author: aknuds1
body:
Translation of OTLP non-monotonic sum metrics has been broken in Prometheus since https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/16626, because [translatorMetricFromOtelMetric](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/16626/files#diff-1e76309731ff41b269672516ed66c8848b751e0d48a596dc8c15a4dda9a2cbecR78) associates sum metric monotonicity with cumulative aggregation temporality. There is no such connection, one should instead (as before that PR) check whether the sum is monotonic. I'm proposing a fix in this PR, and have written a corresponding test in Mimir (see [PR](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/pull/11810)), as a guard against this reoccurring.

I will make an upstream PR, including tests, after this and the Mimir PR get merged.

author: arvinalizadehgithub
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes issue #1051 where PyJWKClient with `cache_keys=True` serves potentially revoked keys indefinitely.

## Problem
When `cache_keys=True` is enabled, PyJWKClient applies `@lru_cache` to the `get_signing_key` method. This caches keys permanently until LRU eviction or process restart. If an identity provider removes a key from their JWKS, applications continue accepting tokens signed with that key.

## Solution
- Replace `lru_cache` with TTL-aware caching
- Keys now expire after the configured `lifespan` (default 300 seconds)
- Maintains full backward compatibility with existing API
- Uses same expiration logic as existing JWKSetCache

## Changes
- **jwt/jwks_client.py**: Replace lru_cache with TTL cache implementation
- **tests/test_jwks_client.py**: Add test demonstrating the fix works

## Testing
All existing tests pass. New test verifies that:
- Old implementation serves cached keys indefinitely
- New implementation properly rejects expired keys

## Backward Compatibility
No breaking changes. All existing parameters work identically:
- `cache_keys=True` still enables individual key caching
- `max_cached_keys` still limits cache size
- Performance characteristics maintained

Fixes #1051

### Review process

If you are an external contributor, you can skip this part. Simply create the pull request, and we'll get back to you as soon as possible.

> This 2-passes review process aims to:
>
> - develop skills of junior reviewers
> - limit the workload for senior reviewers
> - limit the number of unnecessary changes by the _author_

1. The _author_ creates a PR.
2. Review process:
   1. The _author_ assigns the _junior reviewer_.
   2. The _junior reviewer_ conducts their review:
      - Resolves their comments if they are addressed.
      - Adds comments if necessary or approves the PR.
   3. The _junior reviewer_ assigns the _senior reviewer_.
   4. The _senior reviewer_ conducts their review:
      - If there are no unresolved comments on the PR → merge.
      - Otherwise, we continue with **3.**
3. The _author_ responds to comments and/or makes corrections, and we go back to **2.**

Notes:

1. The _author_ can request a review at any time, even if the PR is still a _Draft_.
2. In theory, there should not be more than one reviewer at a time.
3. The _author_ should not make any changes:
   - When a reviewer is assigned.
   - Between the _junior_ and _senior_ reviews.

author: joshmurrayeu
body:
# Summary
Adds optional support for the included block in OpenAPI response schemas generated by buildOpenApiContent.

# Motivation
Our frontend team needs the included block explicitly documented in the OpenAPI schema to enable improved type generation and stricter validation when consuming JSON:API responses.

# Changes
- Signature of buildOpenApiContent() updated to include a third parameter:

```php
bool $included = true
```

- When `$included` is true, the method adds an `'included' => ['type' => 'array']` property to the response schema.
- Defaults to true, maintaining expected behaviour with minimal disruption.

# Impact
- Non-breaking: No effect on existing integrations unless the method is called with $included = false.
- Improves DX for frontend consumers by aligning schema output more closely with actual response structure.

body:
The `_fast_copy` function uses `os.copy_file_range` for efficient copying. However, this function is not available on all platforms such as macOS.

Previously, an uncaught AttributeError would crash the process when the function was missing. By catching AttributeError explicitly and raising _FastCopyFailedFallback, we trigger the existing fallback mechanism for unsupported platforms. This maintains cross-platform compatibility while preserving fast copy operations where supported.

Should be part of 14e1491.

body:
…short

This pull request introduces changes to improve the robustness and flexibility of handling `MessageType` codes by transitioning from `short` to `int`. The primary changes include updating the `MessageType` class to use `int` for code representation, adding a safeguard against duplicate codes, and modifying related methods and usages accordingly.

### Transition from `short` to `int` for `MessageType` codes:

* `collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.java`:
  - Changed the `code` field from `short` to `int` and removed the `intToShort` conversion logic, simplifying the code. (`[collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.javaL52-R66](diffhunk://#diff-359be7b93d56725d0b131e2312bdbc527138bd68568159b03f33227db02c512fL52-R66)`)
  - Updated the `getCode` method to return an `int` instead of a `short`. (`[collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.javaL52-R66](diffhunk://#diff-359be7b93d56725d0b131e2312bdbc527138bd68568159b03f33227db02c512fL52-R66)`)
  - Modified the `getType` method to accept an `int` parameter instead of a `short`. (`[collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.javaL52-R66](diffhunk://#diff-359be7b93d56725d0b131e2312bdbc527138bd68568159b03f33227db02c512fL52-R66)`)

### Safeguard against duplicate `MessageType` codes:

* `collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.java`:
  - Added a check in the `buildMap` method to detect and throw an exception if duplicate `MessageType` codes are encountered. (`[collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/io/util/MessageType.javaL41-R44](diffhunk://#diff-359be7b93d56725d0b131e2312bdbc527138bd68568159b03f33227db02c512fL41-R44)`)

### Updates to dependent code:

* `collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/collector/receiver/AgentDispatchHandler.java`:
  - Updated the `getRequestResponseHandler` method to use `int` for the `type` variable, aligning with the changes in `MessageType`. (`[collector/src/main/java/com/navercorp/pinpoint/collector/receiver/AgentDispatchHandler.javaL63-R63](diffhunk://#diff-7f876b0f18a56422714e54828f5a92ade32a0d7988644c5399c3abb01affbb79L63-R63)`)

author: ank4n
body:
Changes to pallet-staking-async

## Removed
- Config constant `MaxDisabledValidators`: This constant was removed since validator disabling logic has been moved to pallet-session, making it redundant in staking-async.
- Storage DoubleMap `NominatorSlashInEra`: This was used to track per-era maximum slashes for nominators. It’s no longer required — we now only track the highest slash per validator per era.
- Call `withdraw_overstake`: This was a temporary extrinsic meant to fix overstake issues, but with fungible migration of staking funds, this is no longer possible and the extrinsic is obsolete.

## Changed
- Nominator slashing logic: The logic now aggregates slashes from distinct offending validators nominated by a nominator within the same era. For repeated offences by the same validator, only the highest slash fraction is applied. Previously, the pallet applied only the highest slash across all validators, regardless of how many were slashed.

author: krikera
body:
## Summary

Fixes missing blank lines before decorated classes that follow functions in `.pyi` (stub) files.

**Problem**: When a decorated class follows a function definition in a stub file, the formatter was incorrectly omitting the blank line before the class, resulting in formatting like:

```python
def hello(): ...
@decorator
class A: ...
```

**Solution**: Removed the `class_decorator_instead_of_empty_line` condition that was preventing blank lines from being inserted in this scenario. This condition was based on a Black quirk that was actually a bug and shouldn't be replicated.

The fix is gated behind preview mode to ensure backward compatibility. When preview mode is enabled, decorated classes following functions now correctly get blank lines:

```python
def hello(): ...

@decorator
class A: ...
```

This brings Ruff's behavior in line with proper Python style guidelines and fixes the inconsistency where blank lines were added for other statement types but not decorated classes.

## Test Plan

**Manual Testing:**
- Created test files with functions followed by decorated classes
- Verified fix works with `--preview` flag: `cargo run --bin ruff_python_formatter -- --emit stdout --preview test.pyi`
- Verified backward compatibility without `--preview`: old behavior preserved
- Tested with various decorator types (`@lambda`, `@final`, multiple decorators)

**Automated Testing:**
- Added new test case `decorated_class_after_function.pyi` with preview options
- Ran `cargo test -p ruff_python_formatter` - all tests pass
- Snapshot tests show correct formatting changes for both new and existing test cases
- Existing functionality unaffected (no regressions)

**Preview Mode Integration:**
- Added `is_blank_line_before_decorated_class_in_stub_enabled()` preview function
- Verified condition is only applied when preview mode is disabled
- Confirmed proper gating follows established preview patterns

Closes #18865

author: danieltrt
body:
Concrete syntax has a hacky implementation based on string matching. If we want to expand the grammar to support constraints and other constructs, it's worthwhile to build a proper grammar. This will allow us to expand it in the future to use things like:

- `where len(:[name]) > 2` for example to select nodes only with two or more children;
-  `where :[name] matches regex` with regex to add constraints on template variables.

In this PR I essentially wrote the paper, but didn't touch the matching algorithm. In summary:

- Added Pest grammar (concrete_syntax.pest)
- Added parser that converts strings to build an actual AST
- Moved the matching algorithm to [interpreter.rs](https://github.com/danieltrt/piranha/blob/a993eb15fd9f2317f928c6a94c96577ffb73336d/src/models/concrete_syntax/interpreter.rs#L44)

author: anthony4m
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive semantic analysis framework for the `mars` package. It includes the implementation of an `Analyzer` for semantic analysis, along with supporting components like a `SymbolTable`, `TypeChecker`, and `ImmutabilityChecker`. Additionally, it adds test coverage for the analyzer and updates the AST structure to include source code position tracking for enhanced error reporting.

### Semantic Analysis Framework:

* **`mars/analyzer/analyzer.go`**: Implements the `Analyzer` class for semantic analysis, including declaration collection, type checking, and immutability analysis. It introduces methods for handling variable, function, struct, and unsafe block declarations, as well as error reporting for semantic issues like type mismatches and duplicate declarations.

* **`mars/analyzer/symbols.go`**: Adds a `SymbolTable` for managing scopes and symbols. This enables tracking variable, function, and struct declarations across different scopes and resolving symbols during analysis.

* **`mars/analyzer/types.go`**: Introduces a `TypeChecker` skeleton for verifying type compatibility during semantic analysis. While the detailed implementation is deferred, it lays the groundwork for type inference and compatibility checks.

* **`mars/analyzer/immutable.go`**: Provides an initial implementation of an `ImmutabilityChecker` for verifying assignment and mutation rules. This ensures adherence to immutability constraints in the language.

### Test Coverage:

* **`mars/analyzer/analyzer_test.go`**: Adds unit tests for the `Analyzer`, covering variable, function, and struct declaration collection. These tests validate the correctness of symbol resolution and error handling during semantic analysis.

### AST Enhancements:

* **`mars/ast/ast.go`**: Updates the AST structure to include a `Position` field in various nodes (e.g., `Program`, `VarDecl`, `FuncDecl`, `StructDecl`). This enables precise error reporting by tracking line and column information for each node. body:
This PR makes the hangup button visually distinctive by applying a red background color to indicate its destructive action, improving user experience and following modern UI conventions.

## Changes Made

- Updated the hangup button in `UI/Pages/DialerPage.xaml` to use the existing `HangUpButtonStyle` instead of `ActionButtonStyle`
- Removed the explicit orange background color (`#E67E22`) since the style provides the proper red background (`#E74C3C`)

## Before vs After

| **Before** | **After** |
|------------|-----------|
| Orange hangup button (`#E67E22`) using `ActionButtonStyle` | Red hangup button (`#E74C3C`) using `HangUpButtonStyle` |
| Not visually distinctive from other action buttons | Clearly indicates destructive action |

## Benefits

✅ **Better Visual Hierarchy**: The red color makes the hangup button immediately recognizable as a critical action  
✅ **UI Consistency**: Matches the red decline button in the incoming call window (`#E74C3C`)  
✅ **Modern Conventions**: Follows standard UI patterns where destructive actions use red colors  
✅ **Accessibility**: Maintains proper contrast with white text on red background  
✅ **Hover Effects**: Inherits appropriate opacity changes for better user feedback  

## Technical Details

The implementation leverages existing styling infrastructure:
- Uses the pre-existing `HangUpButtonStyle` defined in `App.xaml` 
- Inherits from `ModernButtonStyle` for consistent hover/press effects
- No new styles or colors introduced - minimal, surgical change

This change ensures users can quickly identify the call termination button, reducing the risk of accidental actions and improving the overall user experience.

Fixes #75.

author: derpbravely
body:
## Description

We run out of snapshots on Chromatic too fast. 

This PR proposes that we run chromatic only for snapshot testing (on demand for feature branch PRs and automatically on dev and main)

## Changes

Revert some Storybook/Chromatic changes:
- Only run chromatic builds on commit message "[run-chromatic]" or push to dev/main
- Host Storybook on gh-pages

## Additional Information

The original thesis was that the chromatic setting `onlyStoryNames` could help us reduce the amount of snapshots, after doing some math I released it would only help if a change affects 54 or more stories, which should be rare:

Total stories: `206`
Total components: `42`
a Turbosnap is worth 1/5 of a regular snapshot

A build with the `onlyStoryNames` setting and 1 kitchen sink story per component = `42 + 206 * 0.2 = 83`
A build with the `onlyChanged` setting affecting 15 stories = `15 + (206 - 15) * 0.2 = 53`
A build with the `onlyChanged` setting affecting 54 stories = `54 + (206 - 54) * 0.2 = 84`

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added if applicable
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [x] Conventional commit messages

author: alex-izquierdo
body:
Some refactoring in validators. Some of them are not used anymore or they do check for the existence of the DB by fetching the record, which is inefficient. DRF validators are expected to raise `ValidationError` or return None.  In case of the `organization_id` has been created a mixin to avoid code duplication. 

Refactored:
- organization
- rulebook
- credential_type
- awx_token

Removed:
- event_streams
- extra_vars

Technically, in most of the cases a PrimaryKey field would be better, but that would require a more extended refactor to keep 100% backward compatibility, since we would have to implement custom error messages among other changes. There are multiple fields candidate to be a PrimaryKeyField and such a conversion is not the scope of this PR. 
Here I only address the fields where we are duplicating DB queries, duplicating field definition and removing unused validators.

author: copilot
body:
Railway deployments were failing with `Error: Could not load --schema from provided path prisma/schema.prisma: file or directory not found`. This issue was causing repeated deployment failures and preventing the application from starting.

## Root Cause

The repository contained a symlink at `/prisma` pointing to `server/prisma`. Railway's deployment environment doesn't handle symlinks properly, causing Prisma CLI commands to fail when trying to resolve the schema file path.

```bash
# The problematic symlink structure
/prisma -> server/prisma

# Railway config expected this to work:
# root = "server"
# npx prisma generate --schema=./prisma/schema.prisma
# But symlink resolution failed in deployment environment
```

## Solution

1. **Removed the problematic symlink** that was causing path resolution confusion
2. **Enhanced Railway build process** to ensure proper dependency installation
3. **Updated documentation** with troubleshooting guidance for future issues

## Changes Made

- **Removed** `/prisma` symlink that pointed to `server/prisma`
- **Enhanced** `railway.toml` build command for better validation
- **Added** troubleshooting section to `RAILWAY.md` documenting this issue
- **Verified** all Prisma paths resolve correctly without symlink confusion

## Testing

Verified that:
- ✅ Schema file exists at correct location: `server/prisma/schema.prisma`
- ✅ Railway working directory correctly set to `server/`
- ✅ Relative path `./prisma/schema.prisma` resolves properly
- ✅ No symlink confusion in deployment environment

The deployment should now succeed since Prisma can properly locate the schema file without symlink issues.

Fixes #54.

author: kobayurii
body:
This pull request introduces a new transaction emulation feature and makes several related updates to the codebase. The changes include adding support for transaction emulation in the `CodeStorage` struct, updating the `run_contract` function to handle emulation, and modifying the RPC server to expose the new functionality. Below is a breakdown of the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Transaction Emulation Support

* Added new fields (`tx_actions_collector`, `tx_actions`, `tx_storage`, and `is_tx_emulator`) to the `CodeStorage` struct to support transaction emulation. These fields enable tracking and storing transaction actions and states during emulation. (`rpc-server/src/modules/queries/contract_runner/code_storage.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489R24-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489R57-R60) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489R85-R98)

* Implemented logic in `CodeStorage` methods (`storage_set`, `storage_remove`, `storage_has_key`, and others) to handle transaction emulation by interacting with the new `tx_storage` field. These methods emulate storage operations and track actions when `is_tx_emulator` is enabled. (`rpc-server/src/modules/queries/contract_runner/code_storage.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489L145-R190) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489R202-R213) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d46cbab04673c72199236ec23bc8e3b71e7d30746b26fbdf62b81b28da6489L178-R252)

* Added a new `push_action` method in `CodeStorage` to record transaction actions into `tx_actions` and optionally notify a collector. (`rpc-server/src/modules/queries/contract_runner/code_storage.rs`)

### RPC Server Enhancements

* Introduced a new RPC method, `emulate_tx`, in the `rpc_handler` function to expose the transaction emulation feature to external clients. (`rpc-server/src/main.rs`)

* Updated the `run_contract` function to accept `tx_actions_collector` and `is_tx_emulation` parameters. These changes allow the function to execute contracts in emulation mode when requested. (`rpc-server/src/modules/queries/contract_runner/mod.rs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-766e965c12c4736980def0b4c3a87d7e60c172c27a615c35e824573350022baeL66-R75) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-766e965c12c4736980def0b4c3a87d7e60c172c27a615c35e824573350022baeR183-R189)

### Dependency Updates

* Added the `node-runtime` dependency to `Cargo.toml` files to support the new transaction emulation functionality. (`Cargo.toml`, `rpc-server/Cargo.toml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2e9d962a08321605940b5a657135052fbcef87b5e360662bb527c96d9a615542R60) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a8a1e65c477bdedb3d6a7d6a30eae3153263481b09044f1211bd79f9f16e03caR49)

### Code Refactoring

* Refactored the `RunContractResponse` struct to include additional fields (`block_height` and `block_hash`) for better context in contract execution results. (`rpc-server/src/modules/queries/contract_runner/mod.rs`)

These changes collectively enhance the system by enabling transaction emulation, which can be useful for testing and debugging smart contract interactions without affecting the actual blockchain state.

While trying to set up Lotman in a production setting, I noticed a regression that caused all lot usage to be attributed to the default lot. After some debugging, I discovered a comment in the Lotman source that handles "directory-based usage updates" that indicated Lotman does not expect to have a trailing '/', but this is exactly how the federation-supplied namespace paths were being initialized in lotman.

I view this more as a Lotman bug, but in the interest of getting this moving I'm trimming the '/' in Pelican for now.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR enhances UDP connect redirect tests to properly validate the `bpf_set_redirect_context` API by implementing Windows WFP redirect context retrieval for UDP sockets.

## Problem

The UDP connect redirect tests were unable to validate whether the BPF `bpf_set_redirect_context` API was working correctly because:

1. **Stub implementation**: UDP `query_redirect_context()` was a placeholder that always returned failure
2. **Wrong receive method**: UDP sockets used `WSARecvFrom` instead of `WSARecvMsg`, preventing access to ancillary data
3. **Missing socket option**: UDP sockets didn't enable `IP_WFP_REDIRECT_CONTEXT` to receive redirect context
4. **Limited test expectations**: Tests only expected redirect context validation for TCP connections

## Solution

### Core Implementation Changes

**Modified `_datagram_server_socket` class:**
- Added `control_buffer` and `recv_msg` members for ancillary data handling
- Set `IP_WFP_REDIRECT_CONTEXT` socket option in constructor for UDP sockets
- Replaced `WSARecvFrom` with `WSARecvMsg` to receive control messages
- Implemented proper redirect context extraction from `WSACMSGHDR` structures

**Enhanced test validation:**
- Extended `connect_redirect_tests.cpp` to expect redirect context for `UNCONNECTED_UDP` connections
- Fixed inverted logic bug in `tcp_udp_listener.cpp` for redirect context handling
- Added proper null termination and error handling

### Key Technical Details

```cpp
// Enable redirect context for UDP sockets
if (protocol == IPPROTO_UDP) {
    DWORD option_value = 1;
    setsockopt(socket, IPPROTO_IP, IP_WFP_REDIRECT_CONTEXT, 
               reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&option_value), sizeof(option_value));
}

// Use WSARecvMsg to receive ancillary data
recv_msg.Control = wsa_control_buffer;
error = receive_message(socket, &recv_msg, nullptr, &overlapped, nullptr);

// Extract redirect context from control messages
WSACMSGHDR* cmsg = WSA_CMSG_FIRSTHDR(&recv_msg);
while (cmsg != nullptr) {
    if (cmsg->cmsg_level == IPPROTO_IP && cmsg->cmsg_type == IP_WFP_REDIRECT_CONTEXT) {
        memcpy(buffer, WSA_CMSG_DATA(cmsg), context_size);
        return 0; // Success
    }
    cmsg = WSA_CMSG_NXTHDR(&recv_msg, cmsg);
}
```

## Validation

The changes enable UDP redirect tests to:
- ✅ Validate that `bpf_sock_addr_set_redirect_context()` successfully sets redirect context
- ✅ Retrieve redirect context via Windows WFP mechanisms (`IP_WFP_REDIRECT_CONTEXT`)
- ✅ Distinguish between redirected and non-redirected UDP connections in tests
- ✅ Properly handle `REDIRECT_CONTEXT_MESSAGE` for UDP connections

## Backward Compatibility

- All existing TCP functionality is preserved
- UDP functionality is enhanced, not replaced
- No breaking changes to public APIs
- Maintains existing error handling patterns

## Files Modified

- `tests/libs/util/socket_helper.h` - Added UDP control message members
- `tests/libs/util/socket_helper.cpp` - Implemented WSARecvMsg and redirect context extraction
- `tests/tcp_udp_listener/tcp_udp_listener.cpp` - Fixed redirect context logic
- `tests/connect_redirect/connect_redirect_tests.cpp` - Extended test expectations for UDP

Fixes #2853.

body:
### Overview
This PR introduces basic plotting functionality for the delnx project. It includes:


🧬 dx.pl.volcano_plot: For visualizing differential expression results
🧪 dx.pl.matrix_plot: For summarizing gene expression across categories
📊 dx.pl.gsea_barplot: For visualizing gene set enrichment results

### Details
- Plotting configuration and structure are adapted from scanpy, with the aim of maintaining a familiar API and consistent look.
- The goal was to get minimal but useful visualizations working. I kept dependencies and logic simple.
- There’s likely more to strip away or simplify from scanpy’s architecture (e.g., class wrappers, redundancy), but the current implementation works well in practice for my use case.

### Motivation

body:
This PR transitions the GitHub Actions workflow from Service Principal authentication (with client secrets) to OpenID Connect (OIDC) federated identity for enhanced security when deploying to Azure.

## Changes Made

### GitHub Workflow Updates (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
- **Removed**: `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable (no longer needed)
- **Added**: `ARM_USE_OIDC: true` to enable OIDC authentication
- **Added**: `permissions: id-token: write` to allow OIDC token generation
- **Added**: Explicit Azure login step using `azure/login@v2` with federated credentials

### Documentation Updates

**DEPLOYMENT.md**:
- Updated Azure setup instructions to use App Registration with federated identity instead of Service Principal
- Removed `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` from required GitHub secrets
- Added troubleshooting for federated identity authentication errors
- Enhanced security considerations section

**README.md**:
- Updated prerequisites to show federated identity setup commands
- Removed client secret requirement from GitHub secrets list
- Added security benefits explanation

## Security Benefits

- ✅ **Eliminates long-lived secrets**: No more `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` stored in GitHub
- ✅ **Short-lived tokens**: Uses GitHub's OIDC tokens that expire automatically
- ✅ **Repository-scoped access**: Federated credentials are tied to specific repositories and branches
- ✅ **Reduced attack surface**: Fewer sensitive credentials to manage and rotate

## Migration Path

For existing users, the migration requires:

1. **Azure**: Create App Registration with federated identity credentials
2. **GitHub**: Remove `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` secret (other secrets remain the same)
3. **Repository**: The updated workflow will automatically use OIDC authentication

## Compatibility

- ✅ Terraform infrastructure remains unchanged
- ✅ Deployment functionality preserved
- ✅ All existing workflow triggers and logic maintained
- ✅ Environment protection and approval flows unaffected

## Example Federated Identity Setup

```bash
# Create app registration
az ad app create --display-name "logic-app-deployment-oidc"

# Configure federated credential
az ad app federated-credential create --id $APP_ID --parameters '{
  "name": "github-actions-main",
  "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
  "subject": "repo:YOUR_USERNAME/azuresamples-vm-availability-logicapp:ref:refs/heads/main",
  "audiences": ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]
}'
```

Fixes #5.

author: ivansete-status
body:
## Description

This PR is inspired by a conversation with @NagyZoltanPeter :raised_hands: 

Libwaku implements an event-driven approach, based on callbacks that are passed.

The Waku SDK integrator will implement his/her own callback and hence, given that each callback will be actually invoked by _The Waku Thread_, we incur in the risk of blocking the _Waku Thread_ if the callback's body is not well implemented.

Therefore, this PR suggests the creation of a new possible event: _waku_not_responding_, which will be raised if the _Waku Thread_ is blocked somewhere, either at the integrator's codebase, or in the nwaku's codebase.

To achieve that, a new thread (watchdog) is created, which is aimed to be super simple.

(The idea is also inspired by a typical UI app, such as Discord, or any Android app. In Android, if the main UI thread is blocked for too long, then an ANR event is dispatched.)

## Issue

- https://github.com/waku-org/nwaku/issues/3236

body:
This merge request addresses several critical security vulnerabilities identified in the codebase:

1. **XXE Vulnerabilities in XML Parsing and Transformation**
   - The `DocumentBuilderFactory` is now safely configured to disable external entity processing and disallow DOCTYPE declarations, mitigating XXE attacks.
   - The feature `http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl` is set to `true` before creating the `DocumentBuilder`.
   - The `TransformerFactory` is configured to disable access to external DTDs and stylesheets by setting the attributes `XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET` to empty strings.

2. **Spring Boot Actuator Endpoint Exposure**
   - The configuration exposing all Actuator endpoints (`management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*`) has been restricted or secured to prevent leakage of sensitive information.

After these changes, all previously reported security issues are resolved, and no issues remain. This merge request meaningfully improves the security posture of the application.

body:
This PR addresses code clarity and test coverage issues in the connect redirect test suite by refactoring authorization tests and enhancing redirect test coverage.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Authorization tests incorrectly calling connect_redirect functions
**Problem**: Authorization tests were calling `update_policy_map_and_test_connection()`, which is designed for redirection testing, creating confusion between authorization and redirection functionality.

**Solution**: 
- Created dedicated `authorize_connection_test()` function specifically for authorization testing
- Refactored `authorize_test()` to focus purely on authorization logic (block then allow)
- Removed dependency on redirect-specific functions from authorization tests

### 2. Missing test coverage for both implicit and explicit binds
**Problem**: Connect redirect tests only used explicit binding (specific source address), while authorization tests used implicit binding (wildcard), but there was no comprehensive coverage ensuring both scenarios work for redirect tests.

**Solution**:
- Added `connect_redirect_test_with_implicit_bind_wrapper()` for implicit bind testing
- Enhanced `DECLARE_CONNECTION_REDIRECTION_TEST_FUNCTION` macro to test both binding scenarios
- All redirect tests now run twice: once with explicit bind, once with implicit bind

## Technical Changes

### New Functions
- `authorize_connection_test()`: Dedicated function for testing authorization allow scenarios without redirect logic
- `connect_redirect_test_with_implicit_bind_wrapper()`: Tests redirection with implicit binding (wildcard address)

### Modified Functions
- `authorize_test()`: Now focuses purely on authorization (block/allow) without calling redirect-specific functions
- `DECLARE_CONNECTION_REDIRECTION_TEST_FUNCTION` macro: Enhanced to test both explicit and implicit bind scenarios

## Benefits

- **Separation of Concerns**: Clear distinction between authorization testing and redirection testing
- **Comprehensive Coverage**: All redirection tests now cover both implicit and explicit bind scenarios
- **Code Readability**: Functions have clear, descriptive names and focused responsibilities
- **Maintainability**: Each test type has dedicated helper functions with well-defined purposes

## Testing Impact

- Authorization tests: Test block behavior, then allow behavior with proper audit validation
- Redirection tests: Test both explicit bind (with source address) and implicit bind (wildcard) for complete coverage
- All existing test cases maintained with enhanced functionality

The changes are minimal and surgical, focusing specifically on the identified issues while maintaining backward compatibility and improving test coverage.

Fixes #2868.
