body: ## Description The current implementation of the dxw brand palette is quite jarring. The primary and accent colours are orange and purple, which are roughly opposite each other on the colour wheel, making the homepage in particular high contrast and unattractive for long reading times. The new brand was applied in https://github.com/dxw/advisories/commit/08ccfb6bf0b18385e501a6406b30ce004161ed42 (2022) and described as "a very rough pass to apply the brand". This PR chooses a split-complementary (triadic) set of colours, retaining purple as the main brand colour. In addition we use the teal and pink as accent colours, forming a more balanced and elegant palette. For each primary or accent colour we choose the lightest version, which should be easier to view on web interfaces where visitors may spend longer periods of time. Buttons and the search bar are slightly softer in this PR, and the content fills more horizontal space, but otherwise elements have been largely untouched. Previously, the version of the d-marque that was used on the pages was different to the d-marque in the favicon. This has been fixed here and a wider range of favicons has been provided. There is more on this site overall that could be fixed, but this PR should not introduce new errors. Note: This has already been reviewed by Barry, which is why the number of changes is unusually large. ## How to test 1. Spin up the live site with scripts, note that this site has an internal script which adds site content, but it will leave you with some more widgets on the right hand side of pages than the live site 1. Visit http://localhost/wp-login.php and log in 1. Visit http://localhost/wp-admin/admin.php?page=acf-options-banner and publish a call to action banner with some junk text 1. body:
## Summary
- Added `--no-fail-fast` flag to all cargo test commands in the Makefile
- This ensures all tests run even if some fail, providing complete test results

## Motivation
The `--no-fail-fast` flag is crucial for debugging CI issues. Without it, cargo test stops at the first failing test, which can hide additional failures that might be related to the same root cause. By running all tests regardless of failures, developers get a complete picture of what's broken, making it easier to:

1. Identify patterns in failures
2. Fix multiple related issues at once
3. Understand the full scope of a breaking change
4. Debug flaky tests by seeing all occurrences

This change applies to both test commands in the Makefile:
- `cargo test --no-fail-fast --manifest-path ./crates/cli/Cargo.toml`
- `cargo test --no-fail-fast --all --all-features --exclude sqruff`

## Test plan
- [x] Updated Makefile with --no-fail-fast flags
- [x] CI runs will now show all test failures instead of stopping at the first one

## Summary
Implements the D3 Sub Plan Extractor feature for Phase 4 (EXPORT), providing comprehensive extraction capabilities for substitute planning.

## Key Features Added

### 🚀 Core Extraction Services
- **Weekly Plan Extractor**: Multi-day planning with continuity tracking and weekly overviews
- **Scenario Template Extractor**: 5 emergency scenarios (general, technology failure, severe weather, lockdown, staff shortage)
- **Contact Extractor**: Smart organization of school contacts by priority and category
- **Material Extractor**: Time-based material lists with alternatives and setup instructions

### 📡 API Endpoints (8 new)
- `GET /subplan/extract/weekly` - Extract multi-day plans with continuity
- `GET /subplan/extract/scenarios` - Get emergency scenario templates
- `GET /subplan/extract/contacts` - Extract organized contacts

  - D3 extraction features toggle
  - Scenario condition selectors
  - Live extraction preview
  - Email delivery option

- Updated relationships in User model

- Integration tests for API endpoints

```
extractWeeklyPlan()
├── buildSubPlanData() [for each day]
├── extractWeeklyOverview()
├── generateContinuityNotes()
└── generateEmergencyBackupPlans()

extractScenarioTemplates()

body:
Allow values that were not sent by the Input Model Parameters that were precalculated in WinVDYP to be calculated by the server.

The two instances of this are a crown closure being estimated as the default for the leading species in the event this case is only circumventing the dominant Height check the backend would normally do in that case as WinVDYP would have simply sent the default so the engine could work

The other case is a bit more odd. In the event that no age or height data is sent WnVDYP would assume an age at breast height of 1 use the Supplied SI and Site curve to get a Years to Breast Height value and use that to fill in the Age triplet of age, years to breast height and age at breast height. Then that age would be used for calculating dominant height.  The logic is also only being allowed if the execution option allow aggressive estimation is set

Feed range is now available in the `query_items` API. Users can pass specific feed range to query items.

import json

        enable_cross_partition_query=True,
        feed_range=feed_range,

This PR solves https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/7823 by allowing users to define a DisplayName to be used for OIDC Provider definitions configured via the airbyte helm charts.

<!--

1. **Helm values.yaml**: Added `displayName` field with fallback to `appName`

3. **Application config**: Maps environment variable to `airbyte.auth.identity-provider.oidc.display-name` property
4. **Code injection**: Uses `@Value` annotation to inject the display name into the OIDC configuration
5. **Keycloak setup**: Sets the display name on the identity provider via `idp.setDisplayName()`

5. `airbyte-keycloak-setup/src/main/java/io/airbyte/keycloak/setup/IdentityProvidersConfigurator.java` - takes advantage of the log level improvement in "3" to allow easy inspection of updates to provider definitions when log level is set to DEBUG.

body:
## What is this fixing or adding?
It turned out the Castlevania Advance Collection ROM wasn't working due to the fact that the start inventory hack was overlapping a hack that M2 inserted in the same spot as it in the AC ROM. This fixes support for it by relocating all the start inventory stuff completely (from starting at offset 0x680000 in the ROM to starting at 0x690000).

Note: this does **NOT** fix the audio-related problems that the AC ROM has. That occurs due to it missing its audio-related code.

## How was this tested?
Generated and patched a game with a start inventory using both the cartridge and Advance Collection ROMs and verified both were working and both had the proper start inventory.

author: andrurogerz
body:
## Purpose
This patch is one in a series of code-mods that annotate LLVM’s public interface for export. This patch ensures a few `cl::opt` declarations are properly annotated with `LLVM_ABI`. The annotations currently have no meaningful impact on the LLVM build; however, they are  a prerequisite to support an LLVM Windows DLL (shared library) build.

## Background
This effort is tracked in #109483. Additional context is provided in [this discourse](https://discourse.llvm.org/t/psa-annotating-llvm-public-interface/85307), and documentation for `LLVM_ABI` and related annotations is found in the LLVM repo [here](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/main/llvm/docs/InterfaceExportAnnotations.rst).  

## Overview
- Remove local `extern` declarations of `llvm::PrintPipelinePasses` because it is already correctly declared with an `LLVM_ABI` annotation in `llvm\Passes\PassBuilder.h`. Leaving these declarations results in a gcc compile warning unless they are also annotated with `LLVM_ABI`.
- Similarly, remove local `extern` declarations of `ProfileSummaryCutoffHot` and `UseContextLessSummary` from `llvm/tools/llvm-profgen/ProfileGenerator.cpp` since they are declared with `LLVM_ABI` in `llvm\ProfileData\ProfileCommon.h`.
- Explicitly annotate the extern declaration of `ProfileCorrelate` in `clang/lib/CodeGen/BackendUtil.cpp` since it is not declared in a header. The definition of `ProfileCorrelate` in `llvm\lib\Transforms\Instrumentation\InstrProfiling.cpp` is already annotated with `LLVM_ABI`.

## Validation
Local builds and tests to validate cross-platform compatibility. This included llvm, clang, and lldb on the following configurations:

- Windows with MSVC
- Windows with Clang
- Linux with GCC
- Linux with Clang
- Darwin with Clang

author: zkcosmas
body:
#### 📌 Overview

This PR introduces the initial implementation of **RentalFlow**, a Clarity-based smart contract that enables continuous, real-time rental payments and secure lease lifecycle management for property assets.

#### 🚀 Key Features Implemented

* **Lease Execution & Management**

  * `execute-lease`: Start lease with rent-per-second billing and expiration date.
  * `terminate-lease`: Automatically settle rent and return unused deposit.
  * `pause-rent-collection` & `resume-rent-collection`: Allow temporary pause in rent flow with time-adjusted resumption.

* **Security Vault Mechanism**

  * `deposit-security` & `withdraw-security`: Landlords/tenants can manage locked funds.
  * `add-security-deposit`: Add more collateral during an active lease.

* **Automated Rent Streaming**

  * `calculate-collectible-rent`: Determines real-time rent due from elapsed time.
  * `collect-rent`: Deducts rent from deposits and transfers to landlord vault.

* **Indexing & Property Tracking**

  * `landlord-property-portfolio` and `tenant-rental-history` mappings.
  * `property-statistics`: Tracks total properties and tenancies per user.

* **Read-Only Queries**

  * Lease status, rent calculations, vault balances, expiration checks, and metadata lookups (`get-lease-agreement`, `get-vault-balance`, `has-lease-expired`, etc.).

#### 🧪 Testing & Validation

* Comprehensive state validation via:

  * Lease lifecycle assertions
  * Vault balance checks
  * Rent streaming accuracy with pause/resume flow
* Data consistency for landlords and tenants via indexed mappings

#### ❗ Error Handling

* Centralized error codes like `ERR_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN`, `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_SECURITY`, `ERR_RENT_FROZEN`, etc., for robust access and state validation.

author: rohitrastogi
body:
Instead of using a boolean flag to control whether the similarity score column is included, the API now accepts an optional column name for the similarity score. If similarity_score_column is None, no similarity score is added. If a name is provided, the score is included under that column name.

This design is particularly useful when performing multiple similarity joins or computing embedding distances, as it avoids the need for users to rename columns manually to prevent conflicts. It also aligns with established patterns like with_column, where the user explicitly controls column naming.

author: skamensky
body:
SQL injection vulnerabilities in the Postgres Formula Compiler were addressed by implementing robust escaping and safe SQL construction.

*   In `src/sql-generator.js`, the `FUNCTIONS.DATE` case now escapes single quotes in `expr.value.stringValue` by replacing `'` with `''`, preventing string literal termination.
*   `FUNCTIONS.ADDMONTHS`, `FUNCTIONS.ADDDAYS`, and date arithmetic in `TYPE.BINARY_OP` were refactored. Numeric expressions are no longer embedded within quoted `INTERVAL` strings (e.g., `INTERVAL '${num} days'`). Instead, they use `num * INTERVAL '1 day'` (or `month`), ensuring the numeric part is treated as a value, preventing injection and correcting logical errors.
*   Table names (`baseTableName`, `joinIntent.targetTable`) and join fields in `src/sql-generator.js` are now consistently double-quoted (e.g., `"${baseTableName}"`). This hardens the SQL against identifier-based injection and ensures proper handling of special characters.
*   Existing tests in `tests/date-arithmetic.test.js` and `tests/date-functions.test.js` were updated to match the new secure SQL output. All tests pass, validating the fixes and confirming no regressions.

body:
# Feature: Private Post Audience Selection & Backend Follower API Route

## Description

This pull request introduces a new feature that allows users to select specific followers who can view their private posts. It also fixes the backend API routing to ensure the frontend can fetch the correct list of followers for this feature. Additional minor improvements and configuration updates are included.

---

## Summary of Changes

### Frontend

- **CreatePost.js**
  - When the "Private" privacy option is selected, the component fetches the current user's followers from the backend.
  - A multi-select dropdown is displayed, allowing the user to choose which followers can view the private post.
  - On post submission, the selected follower IDs are sent as `allowed_users` in the API request (only for private posts).
  - Public and almost private post behaviors remain unchanged.

- **.env.local**
  - Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` to `http://localhost:8000` to ensure all frontend API requests are directed to the correct backend server during local development.

- **.gitignore**
  - Updated to ignore Node.js, Next.js, Go, database, Docker, IDE/editor, and build artifact files.
  - Added rules for `.env` files, images, and seed data to prevent accidental commits of sensitive or unnecessary files.

---

### Backend

- **router.go**
  - Registered the `/api/follow/followers/{userId}` endpoint in the `setupFollowRoutes` function.
  - This enables the frontend to fetch a user's followers for features like private post audience selection.

---

## How it Works

- When creating a post, if the user selects "Private" as the privacy level, a list of their followers is fetched and shown.
- The user can select one or more followers who will be able to see the post.
- The backend now properly exposes the followers API endpoint, so the frontend can always retrieve the correct list.
- Other privacy levels (Public, Almost Private) are unaffected and retain their existing behavior.

---

## Checklist

- [x] Follower selection UI for private posts
- [x] Backend route for fetching followers
- [x] API integration between frontend and backend
- [x] Updated environment and ignore files

---

author: liyanjun19
body:
Libraries using Comprise payments reported that donations being made through Aspen are being lumped together with fine payments on Comprise reports. 
To fix this, we can add a separate optional section for Donation, with a different Customer Name and Customer ID. If libraries do not fill out the donation section, the donation will use the general customer name and customer ID.

To Test:
1. Set the payment method to Comprise in Library > Fines/e-commerce > Show E-Commerce Link
2. Set a patron account with $2 fines 
3. Apply this PR, leave Comprise Settings > Donation settings (Optional) as blank 
4. Add a logger for `$paymentRequestUrl` in `code/web/services/MyAccount/AJAX.php` > `createCompriseOrder()`
5. Go to My Account > Fines > Click to pay fines online, in `messages.log` see the $paymentRequestUrl is using the General customer name and customer ID 
6. Try to submit donations, in `messages.log` see the $paymentRequestUrl is using the General customer name and customer ID
7. Go to Comprise Settings > Donation settings (Optional), enter values for Customer Name/ID for Donation (Optional)
8. Try to submit fines again, see $paymentRequestUrl use the General customer name and customer ID 
9. Try to submit donations again, see $paymentRequestUrl use the customer name for Donation and customer ID for Donation
10. Go to Comprise Settings  and remove the values for Customer Name/ID for Donation (Optional)
11. Try to submit fines and donations, see the $paymentRequestUrl use the general customer name and customer ID

# Comprehensive Memory Optimization and Performance Improvements

This PR implements extensive memory optimization and performance improvements across the bookmark system, focusing on reducing memory usage, improving caching strategies, and enhancing error handling.

## 🚀 New Features

* **Lightweight Loading System**: Added LightweightBookmark type and BookmarkLoadOptions interface for memory-efficient bookmark loading that excludes heavy image data
* **Advanced Asset Proxy**: Enhanced asset route with S3 write-through cache, improved timeout handling, and better error recovery with automatic retry logic  
* **Memory-Aware Caching**: Implemented unified image memory management system with LRU cache, memory pressure detection, and automatic cleanup
* **Request Coalescing**: Added deduplication for concurrent asset requests to prevent duplicate fetches

## ⚡ Performance Optimizations  

* **Next.js Data Cache Disabled**: Disabled Next.js default data cache for dynamic content to prevent memory duplication
* **Memory Usage Optimization**: Stripped image data from bookmark responses when not needed, reducing memory footprint
* **Development Mode Optimizations**: Disabled React strict mode in development, optimized webpack cache configuration, and reduced parallelism
* **Filesystem Cache**: Switched to filesystem-based webpack cache in development to dramatically reduce memory usage
* **Cache Efficiency**: Set cacheMaxMemorySize to 0 to disable Next.js built-in cache in favor of custom caching implementation

## 🔧 Infrastructure Improvements

* **Server Cache Enhancements**: Improved server cache implementation with better memory management and cleanup strategies
* **Image Memory Manager**: Centralized image buffer handling with size limits (50MB per image, 512MB total budget) and TTL-based eviction
* **Data Fetch Manager**: Enhanced with memory-aware request handling and better resource cleanup
* **OpenGraph Script Optimization**: Optimized refresh-opengraph-images script for reduced memory usage during batch operations

## 🛠️ Code Quality & Type Safety

* **Enhanced Type Definitions**: Added comprehensive Zod schemas for bookmark assets, loading options, and lightweight bookmark types
* **Improved Error Handling**: Better AWS error type interfaces with proper metadata property typing
* **ESLint Configuration**: Updated ESLint config and integrated Biome into core validation script
* **Test Reliability**: Added proper cleanup in test files to prevent side effects between test runs

## 🧪 Test Improvements

* **Console Restoration**: Added afterEach hooks to restore console.log after tag filtering tests
* **Enhanced Test Data**: Updated tag objects in tests to include id and slug attributes for better type coverage
* **Type Safety**: Replaced unsafe any type assertions with proper AWS error type interfaces

## 📁 Files Changed (24 files, +293/-117 lines)

This comprehensive update significantly reduces memory usage while maintaining performance and adds robust error handling throughout the bookmark system.

author: kyrieb-ekat
body:
feat: Add robust model evaluation and classification system with intelligent architecture detection

## New Classification & Testing Scripts

### Core Scripts:
- `fixed_basic_classifier.py`: Single image classification with trained models
- `single_model_tester.py`: Test one model against all images in directory  
- `batch_model_tester.py`: Comprehensive testing of all models vs all images

### Key Features:
- **Robust architecture detection**: Automatically handles global (10-feat), local (8-feat), and legacy models
- **Multiple fallback strategies**: working_dual_pathway → alternative → legacy → image-only
- **Comprehensive output formats**: CSV with class probabilities, JSON with metadata, summary reports
- **Memory efficient**: Models cleared between tests to prevent memory issues

## Architecture Compatibility:
- ✅ Global models (anti_overfitting_global_training.py) - 10 features
- ✅ Local models (fixed_robust_training.py) - 8 features  
- ✅ Legacy models with alternative layer naming (features_dense_1)
- ✅ Image-only models as final fallback

## Output Format:
CSV results provide "Model → Image → Classifications" with:
- Individual class probabilities (st_gall_prob, hispanic_prob, beneventan_prob, square_prob)
- Confidence scores and success indicators
- Model type detection (global/local/standard)
- Batch analysis reports for performance comparison

## Validation Results:
- ✅ Successfully loads models with 98.83% accuracy from comprehensive_model_analysis.py
- ✅ Correctly handles difficult manuscripts with appropriate uncertainty
- ✅ Demonstrates sophisticated paleographic analysis (e.g., St. Gall layout + Square notation → Square)
- ✅ Robust performance across different model architectures and training methods

## Dependencies:
- Requires working_dual_pathway.py and config.py in classifier directory
- Compatible with existing training pipeline outputs
- Handles mixed model types in single batch run

Fixes architecture loading issues that prevented evaluation of models with different feature dimensions and layer naming conventions.

author: mmccrackan
body:
In the noise fitting, python warnings are converted into errors so they can catch failure cases for the Q/U fitting when there is little 1/f.  This PR just ensures that this change is scoped.  The current approach changes the warnings to errors globally, so all warnings will cause a runtime error.

Tested by running the PSD calc process with `full_output = False`, which raises a warning and it now does not result in a `RuntimeError` exit and all fit failure logging statements are preserved.

author: damccorm
body:
Ordering was introduced into this workflow to prevent race conditions as multiple jobs write to svn. However, the wrong ordering was applied, and staging python and prism to svn are blocked on pushing java artifacts to maven instead of the job that pushes java artifacts to svn.

This currently works because publishing to maven takes much longer than the svn step, so the ordering is effectively maintained, but it means that it takes way longer for python/go artifact publishing to start, lengthening the overall job run time and making it expensive to deal with failures.

This fixes the problem

author: alexcrichton
body:
This commit extracts the `wasm-tools json-from-wast` subcommand to its own dedicated crate. This namely creates a Rust-typed AST for the JSON encoding which uses types more liberally in various locations instead of stringly-typed things. The intention is to make it easier to consume `*.json` files in Rust projects (like Wasmtime using Miri).

This started with a goal of not changing the output of any `*.json` tests but in integrating this into Wasmtime I found a few minor mistakes which needed updating anyway so some slight adjustments were made along the way to some JSON bits.

author: ngoldbaum
body:
c.f. #1784.

This PR updates the tests to be runnable in a thread pool under pytest-run-parallel. It then makes use of pytest-run-parallel to do multithreaded testing on the free-threaded build in CI.

The updates to the tests are mostly to avoid sharing filesystem paths between test runners. I also marked all the multiprocessing tests as thread-unsafe because they rely on `fork` and they rely on mutating `os.environ`.

To avoid running into runtime borrow-checker errors, I wrapped the internal state of the `PyEncoder` pyclass in a `Mutex`. I don't think it's possible for any panics to happen while mutexes are locked that weren't already possible and in all cases I think it's correct to immediately propagate panics with `unlock()` rather than trying to handle poisoned mutexes.

body:
## User-Facing Changes
Lichtblick now enforces a minimum width for the left sidebar to ensure all four tabs are always visible. This prevents tabs from being hidden when the sidebar is resized.

## Description
- A minimum width of 240 pixels has been enforced for the left sidebar.
- Since `react-mosaic-component` only supports percentage-based sizing, a direct CSS solution (e.g. `min-width`) was not feasible.
- Instead, the logic intercepts and clamps the sidebar size in the relevant handlers to prevent it from shrinking below the required threshold.

- The `Sidebar` component was also cleaned up by removing unused code related to the legacy left-hand sidebar, which is no longer in use.

- [x] The desktop version was tested and it is running ok

author: scylladbbot
body:
optimized_clang.sh trains the compiler using profile-guided optimization (pgo). However, while doing that, it builds scylladb using its own profile stored in pgo/profiles and decompressed into build/profile.profdata. Due to the funky directory structure used for training the compiler, that path is invalid during the training and the build fails.

The workaround was to build on a cloud machine instead of a workstation - this worked because the cloud machine didn't have git-lfs installed, and therefore did not see the stored profile, and the whole mess was averted.

To make this work on a machine that does have access to stored profiles, disable use of the stored profile even if it exists.

Fixes #22713

Marking for backport; while it's just an inconvenience, it's a big time waster in case we have to regenerate the toolchain on a branch.

- (cherry picked from commit 52f11e140f2ed86326c0f149c525c013454bd141)

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
# Integrate Movie Data Fetching and MovieCard Enhancements

## Overview

This PR introduces several key features and improvements to the movie browsing experience, including:

- Fetching trending movies using the TMDB API.
- Fetching detailed movie info using the OMDB API by IMDb ID.
- Utility functions for consistent and safe API interactions.
- A refactored `MovieCard` component with helper methods and graceful fallbacks.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. **API Integration**
- Implemented `fetchFromTMDB` to handle TMDB API calls with dynamic query params and error handling.
- Created `getMovieDetails` to fetch detailed movie data from OMDB using an IMDb ID.

### 2. **Homepage Updates**
- Added logic to fetch and display top 8 trending movies from TMDB.
- Included loading and error states with retry capability.
- Added placeholder sections for future TV show integration.

### 3. **MovieCard Component Refactor**
- Extracted logic into helper functions:
  - `getPosterUrl()`
  - `getReleaseYear()`
  - `getTitle()`
  - `getRating()`
- Added graceful fallbacks for missing data (e.g., title, release date, rating).
- Improved image error handling to use a placeholder on load failure.

---

##  UI Updates

- Styled movie cards now display consistently even with incomplete data.
- Spinner shown while loading; error messages with retry option.
- Clear separation between movies and placeholder TV section.

---

## Testing

- Verified TMDB and OMDB data fetches.
- Confirmed correct rendering and fallbacks for various edge cases.
- Confirmed image fallback behavior when poster is missing or broken.

---

## Notes

- TV show data section is currently a placeholder.
- Environment variables `VITE_TMDB_API_KEY` and `VITE_OMDB_API_KEY` must be set to run this feature correctly.

---

##  Related Commits

- `Add utility functions to fetch movie details from OMDB and TMDB APIs`
- `Fetch and display trending movies from TMDB API on homepage`
- `Refactor MovieCard to use helper functions for title, poster, release year, and rating`

---

##  Ready for Review

This feature is complete and ready for code review and testing. Feedback and suggestions are welcome!

author: scylladbbot
body:
optimized_clang.sh trains the compiler using profile-guided optimization (pgo). However, while doing that, it builds scylladb using its own profile stored in pgo/profiles and decompressed into build/profile.profdata. Due to the funky directory structure used for training the compiler, that path is invalid during the training and the build fails.

The workaround was to build on a cloud machine instead of a workstation - this worked because the cloud machine didn't have git-lfs installed, and therefore did not see the stored profile, and the whole mess was averted.

To make this work on a machine that does have access to stored profiles, disable use of the stored profile even if it exists.

Fixes #22713

Marking for backport; while it's just an inconvenience, it's a big time waster in case we have to regenerate the toolchain on a branch.

- (cherry picked from commit 52f11e140f2ed86326c0f149c525c013454bd141)

author: mmdriley
body:
This should get us a version that is built with/against more recent versions of Cargo, which will in turn fix the error we're seeing in CI:

```
error: failed to parse manifest at `/home/runner/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/base64ct-1.8.0/Cargo.toml`

Caused by:
  feature `edition2024` is required

  The package requires the Cargo feature called `edition2024`, but that feature is not stabilized in this version of Cargo (1.83.0).
  Consider trying a more recent nightly release.
```

We could also use `cargo install` but it is *very* slow (4m).

This change also updates all uses of `checkout@v2` to `checkout@v4`. Unfortunately, this is **not** just an unrelated cleanup: `checkout@v4` [stores an access token in the local Git repo config](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/09d2acae674a48949e3602304ab46fd20ae0c42f/README.md#checkout-v4), which in turn [gets picked up by `cargo-binstall`](https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall/blob/8aac5aa2bf0dfaa2863eccad9f43c68fe40e5ec8/crates/bin/src/args.rs#L384-L386) so it can access the Github REST API. Without the update, `cargo binstall` fails and falls back to compiling from source.
